structured.approach: I followed the data-science-steps DS-04 procedure. First I read the six contracted inputs and the ap_forecast code (the tool view plus ci.py). Then I used context_list to confirm that the DS-02 (task.secrets_scope) and DS-03 (task.db_changes) outputs are approved background, and read both to answer the secrets question for every environment. A draft from an earlier attempt was already at the output path. I read it and rewrote it in full. In the rewrite I corrected its task.repo_access revision (aac590a, not c7b4be8), its swapped RAQ-1/RAQ-2 references, and its unchecked secrets row, which now cites DS-02. A verifier subagent then flagged 4 problems: background hashes with no source, a memory claim that contradicted feat.tasks section 8, an uncited docstring suggestion, and a wrong section reference. It also flagged an inference about coverage that was not marked as such. I fixed all of these. No shell commands were run, because the G9 hook allows none in DS-04.

claims.text: The Data Science lane changes only ap_forecast, for TSK-03 (STORY-03) and TSK-04 (STORY-04).

Create src/ap_forecast/risk.py with HIGH_ABOVE_DAYS = 30, MEDIUM_ABOVE_DAYS = 10 and vendor_risk(history). It calls predict_delay_days once and compares with strict '>'. It imports only predict_delay_days, not explain.
Update src/ap_forecast/__init__.py: import vendor_risk, add it to __all__, and take one minor version step from 0.9.0. TSK-03 owns the version step.

Update explain.build_explanation_request additively. Add risk=None as the last parameter and append f" Risk level: {risk}." only when risk is not None. Provider, model and max_tokens still come from config or load_config().
Tests: a new tests/test_risk.py with the five vendor_risk tests, and two request tests appended to tests/test_forecast.py. The existing three tests stay unchanged.
predict.py and models.json stay unchanged. models.json holds provider acme-llm, model acme-text-2 and max_tokens 300.

ci.py finds every test under tests/ and measures coverage on src/ap_forecast with COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0. It also runs static checks: no print/eval/exec, no bare except, lines at most 140 characters. So new modules and test files need no CI change.
No secrets are required or granted in CI, feature/<story>, dev or main, and no access request is needed.
No database or Databricks change is needed for the Data Science lane.
Boundary tests use single-value histories [30], [31], [10] and [11], applying lesson L-007.
PROV-ACME-2026-11 also changes build_explanation_request. Whichever change merges second rebases and re-runs T-7. This gates release, not coding.

open_questions: CQ-DS-1: feat.stories TK-03.2 puts the risk tests in tests/test_forecast.py, but feat.tasks (section 2; TA-4) assigns a new tests/test_risk.py. Interim: follow feat.tasks. The Developer confirms under TKQ-2.
CQ-DS-2: What is the exact next version after 0.9.0? Interim: a minor step, value to be confirmed in DS-05.
RAQ-1 (carried): Is the coverage package installed for /usr/bin/python3 on the CI runner? The first CI run will confirm.
RAQ-2 (carried): Should STORY-03 and STORY-04 share the single feature/story branch, or each get its own branch?
structured.summary: I wrote task.components for the ap_forecast Data Science lane. It lists 5 components: create risk.py with vendor_risk and two threshold constants (CMP-1), update __init__.py with the export and version step (CMP-2), add risk=None to explain.py (CMP-3), create tests/test_risk.py (CMP-4), and append two tests to tests/test_forecast.py (CMP-5). predict.py, models.json and ci.py stay unchanged. The file includes minimal code sketches and maps each test to its acceptance criteria. Per the DS-02 and DS-03 outputs, no secrets, database or Databricks are needed in any environment. There are no blocking questions. The verifier's findings have been fixed.
